Core rules implemented and traceable: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - JSDoc header references @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Uses shared helpers from ./helpers/require-story-helpers (DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode, buildVisitors). - meta.schema defines options: scope (enum DEFAULT_SCOPE) and exportPriority (enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES). - meta.messages.missingStory provides a clear, actionable error message, including an example story path. - create(context) wires sourceCode, scope, exportPriority into buildVisitors and shouldProcessNode, ensuring consistent behavior.
- src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - JSDoc header references @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and requirements REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY. - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES from ./helpers/require-story-helpers and uses the same shouldProcessNode helper as require-story-annotation. - meta.schema mirrors require-story-annotation: scope (enum DEFAULT_SCOPE), exportPriority (enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES). - meta.messages.missingReq gives a specific, actionable message including the function name and an example @req tag. - create(context) normalizes options, constructs shouldCheck(node) with shouldProcessNode, and calls checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) for all supported node types.
Shared function detection and scope (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - DEFAULT_SCOPE: ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]. This matches the story's required set of function-like constructs and is used by both rules. - EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES: ["all", "exported", "non-exported"].
- src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES for consumers. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): - Returns false if node.type is not in scope. - Uses isExportedNode to detect ExportNamedDeclaration / ExportDefaultDeclaration ancestors. - Honors exportPriority = "all", "exported", or "non-exported". - isExportedNode walks parent chain defensively to determine export status.
- src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts and src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Both rules share the same scope semantics (DEFAULT_SCOPE) and exportPriority behavior via shouldProcessNode, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY.
JSDoc/comment parsing and common strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts (for @story): - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and checks for "@story". - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and searches for "@story". - leadingCommentsHasStory(node) inspects node.leadingComments. - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) combines jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, and additional helpers linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, all wrapped in try/catch for graceful failure.
- src/utils/annotation-checker.ts (for @req): - getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments provide a parallel abstraction for comments. - commentContainsReq checks for "@req". - linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq mirror the @story detection logic, using LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW constants from helpers. - hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node) uses the same layered heuristics with error handling and then falls back to simple string contains checks. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options) obtains sourceCode, collects comments, calls hasReqAnnotation, and calls reportMissing if no annotation is found.
Annotation enforcement (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED): - require-story-annotation - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts defines visitors for function-like nodes: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, ArrowFunctionExpression. - Each handler first checks options.shouldProcessNode(node) and then calls helperReportMissing or helperReportMethod. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?) checks hasStoryAnnotation; if missing, derives functionName via extractName, resolves an insertion target via resolveTargetNode, and calls context.report with messageId "missingStory", data { name, functionName }, and autofix + suggestion. - reportMethod(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?) does similar for methods, reporting at the method name node and providing fixes.
- require-req-annotation - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts’s create() defines runCheck(node) which uses shouldCheck (built from shouldProcessNode) and invokes checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }). - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) uses getNodeName to derive a readable function name, sets data { name, functionName: name }, and reports with messageId "missingReq". It optionally attaches an autofix via createMissingReqFix when enableFix is true.
TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - require-story-annotation - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts - buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor and buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor implement visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature, calling helperReportMissing with appropriate targets. - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md lists TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature in the supported node types and shows TS examples.
- require-req-annotation - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts visitors include TSDeclareFunction(node) and TSMethodSignature(node) that call runCheck. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts checkReqAnnotation is type-agnostic and works with TS ASTs using @typescript-eslint/parser.
Arrow functions excluded by default (part of REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION): - DEFAULT_SCOPE deliberately omits "ArrowFunctionExpression" and is the only allowed scope value set in both rules’ schemas. - require-story-annotation: - Has an ArrowFunctionExpression visitor, but shouldProcessNode will return false under the default scope, so arrow functions are not enforced unless scope is explicitly broadened in the future. - require-req-annotation: - Has no ArrowFunctionExpression visitor, so arrow functions are not checked. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts includes a valid case named "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" with code `const arrowFn = () => {};`, confirming arrow functions are excluded by default.
Error location & user experience (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and UX criteria): - require-story-annotation - extractName(node) in require-story-helpers.ts walks Identifier nodes, id, key, and name properties to derive a meaningful name, falling back to "(anonymous)". - reportMissing uses nameNode derived from node.id or node.key (Identifier) or node itself; this anchors the lint error to the function name where available. - Error message for missingStory: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story..." – concise, imperative, and clearly tells the developer what to do. - tests/rules/require-story-core-edgecases.test.ts includes a test that calls reportMissing with a fake sourceCode missing getJSDocComment, verifies context.report is still called, and asserts the node and messageId, covering error-location and malformed-source handling.
- require-req-annotation - reportMissing in annotation-checker.ts uses getNodeName to derive function names, and chooses nameNode as the id/key Identifier when possible, otherwise node – aligning error locations with function identifiers. - Error message for missingReq: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE')..." – specific and includes guidance and format.
Graceful error handling (Acceptance Criterion: Error Handling): - hasStoryAnnotation and report* in require-story-helpers.ts wrap potentially fragile operations (AST introspection, comment and text scanning) in try/catch and swallow errors, treating failures as "no annotation" rather than crashing ESLint. - annotation-checker.ts similarly wraps advanced heuristics (linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq, sourceCode access) in try/catch, with comments explaining the intent to fail gracefully. - tests/rules/require-story-core-edgecases.test.ts explicitly exercises reportMissing when sourceCode is missing getJSDocComment, ensuring no runtime error and a proper report call.

traceability.notes: All key acceptance criteria for story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied. The plugin implements two coordinated ESLint rules, require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation, that operate over the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) with arrow functions explicitly excluded by default. Both rules share configurable scope and exportPriority semantics via common helpers, provide robust JSDoc/comment and source-text based detection for @story/@req annotations, support TypeScript-specific nodes, and anchor errors at the function or method name with clear, actionable messages. Extensive RuleTester suites and edge-case tests trace back to this story and verify enforcement, configuration behavior, error reporting, and error-handling resilience. Rule documentation exists with examples and configuration details. On this basis, the implementation of this story is assessed as PASSED.
